structs.name: GfxShaderTextureRWView
structs.size_evidence: method 4 (array stride) + method 3 (whole-object init): R_DispatchTextureViewBatch@0x14188d230 walks its RW-view array with `v8 += 4` (qwords = 32 bytes), calling R_AssignNullShaderTextureRWView@0x1418bca10 and R_ReleaseShaderTextureRWView@0x1418be550 on each element; R_AssignNullShaderTextureRWView writes every byte 0..31 (stores at +0, +8, +16, +20, +24, +28). Game-test 24 is contradicted by the +28 stores. Replay max access end 32.
members: R_DispatchTextureViewBatch@0x14188d230: `*v11 = v12` where v12 = *resourceRefs and is the resource argument of CreateUnorderedAccessView (device vtable +152); R_AssignNullShaderTextureRWView: `*(QWORD*)view = 0`. Renamed from IDA m_view: Replay stores the resource here
R_DispatchTextureViewBatch: `v11[1] = 0`, which is the counter-resource argument (0) of the same UAV create; R_AssignNullShaderTextureRWView: `*(QWORD*)(view+8) = 0`. Renamed from IDA m_resource

R_ReleaseShaderTextureRWView@0x1418be550: `R_ReleaseDescriptor(r_globalDescriptorPoolC, *(view+16))`; R_DispatchTextureViewBatch: `*((DWORD*)v11+4) = v13` (freelist slot). The value is a descriptor index, not a format. Renamed from IDA m_format

UNCONFIRMED name: value 3 written at +20 by R_AssignNullShaderTextureRWView (`view+20 = 3`) and by the batch (`*((DWORD*)v11+5) = 3`). It is not the UAV desc ViewDimension (the batch's desc v27[1] is 4). Renamed from IDA m_firstMip (no Replay code uses it as a mip)

R_DispatchTextureViewBatch: `*((DWORD*)v11+6) = v10`, the loop index, which is also the UAV desc MipSlice (`v27[2] = v10`); R_AssignNullShaderTextureRWView writes -1 (null view). Renamed from IDA m_mipCount. Game-test rwSubresourceToTransition (gt +0x14) may be this field: UNCONFIRMED
R_DispatchTextureViewBatch: `*((DWORD*)v11+7) = 0`, which is the UAV desc FirstArraySlice (`v27[3] = 0`); R_AssignNullShaderTextureRWView: `view+28 = 0`. Renamed from IDA m_arraySlice
changed_members: value 3 in both writers; not a mip
batch stores the loop index, which is UAV desc MipSlice
batch stores 0, which is UAV desc FirstArraySlice
unconfirmed: m_mipSlice (+24): game-test rwSubresourceToTransition may be this field, not proven
structs.notes: Every Replay access (+0, +8, +16, +20, +24, +28) is placed; the 4-byte stores cover 0..32 with no gap. Game-test 24 (4 fields: rwResource, rwCounterResource, rwView, rwSubresourceToTransition) is an older layout: Replay's element is 32 bytes. Members are types only as read from the stores; all six are 8/4-byte scalars or pointers as written. Naming follows game-test where Replay code agrees (rwResource, rwCounterResource, rwView, mip, array slice).

structs.name: GfxSurfaceBounds
structs.size_evidence: method 4 (array stride) + loader: R_BspSurf_TestSurfaceBounds@0x1418d2470 computes `imul rcx, rax, 38h` (surfaceIndex * 56) and `add rcx, [rgp_world+0F8h]` (surfaces.surfaceBounds); Load_GfxWorldSurfaces@0x140e305d0 streams `Load_Stream(0, pos, 56LL * surfaceCount)` into varGfxSurfaceBounds. Both give 56-byte elements. IDA size 56 is right; game-test 24 is not proven.
members: R_BspSurf_TestSurfaceBounds@0x1418d2470: `movss xmm, [rcx+0]`, `[rcx+4]`, `[rcx+8]` (midPoint.v[0..2]) and `[rcx+0Ch]`, `[rcx+10h]`, `[rcx+14h]` (halfSize.v[0..2]); Bounds is 24 bytes (vec3 midPoint, vec3 halfSize)
unconfirmed: serializedExtra (+24, 32 bytes, IDA type Replay_SurfaceBoundsExtra = float scalar + unsigned int reserved[7]): space is proven by the 56-byte stride, but no Replay read of +24..+56 was found; the IDA name and type stay UNCONFIRMED and are left as a pad-like tail
structs.notes: Replay's only element reader I found is R_BspSurf_TestSurfaceBounds (reads +0..+24). The collectors that call it (R_BspSurf_CollectSurfaces, CollectCameraSurfaces, CollectSurfacePair, CollectCameraWithMaterials, CollectSurfacesWithMaterial, CollectCameraNoMaterials, and the other R_BspSurf_Collect* functions I scanned) do not index the array themselves. The xrefs to rgp_world are capped at 200 in the tool result, so an unseen reader cannot be fully excluded; that is the only limit on the +24..+56 tail. Replay_SurfaceBoundsExtra is a local type with no Replay evidence.
